source.title: In-Context Fixation: When Demonstrated Labels Override Semantics in Few-Shot Classification

record.file_problem: Minor PDF-to-text layout and character artifacts; the study text is otherwise complete.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses induction heads and proposes that its label-fixation result is consistent with a generalized induction mechanism, but it does not test induction-head formation, the [A][B] … [A] → [B] behavior, training-time formation, or the claimed relationship to token-index in-context learning.
record.gate_note: The paper measures label fixation and patches activations to study that failure mode. Those results do not measure the induction-head behavior or training dynamics named by V1–V7. The induction-head interpretation and comparisons to prior work are discussion, not a direct test of those versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures label fixation in few-shot classification and patches attention layers/heads mediating it. It never identifies induction heads (no prefix-matching/copying scores, no previous-token composition), has no training-time data, and does not measure token-index ICL. Its induction-head statements are interpretive discussion, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ICL output in this regime is constrained retrieval from the demonstrated label-slot inventory, implemented by an encode-then-override attention circuit. They call this consistent with a generalized induction mechanism retrieving a position- and frequency-weighted set, and argue single-token false-induction-head copying cannot explain the varied-nonsense result. Both points are interpretation, not a measurement of induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates label fixation with activation patching and probability measurements; it does not reproduce the original induction-head method.
record.method_sensitivity: For label fixation, the paper reports sensitivity to demonstrated-label diversity and position: varied labels redistribute probability within the demonstrated set, and a corrective demonstration at position 8 reverses fixation whereas one at position 1 has zero effect. These are not induction-head measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four base models, varied nonsense demonstration labels put 42–67% of probability on the demonstrated set with P(dog)<0.2%; homogeneous nonsense labels are copied with >92% probability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In few-shot classification, model output is restricted to the demonstrated label-token inventory even when labels are nonsense (set-level label fixation).

fits_no_version.finding: Paired attention-layer patching recovers 98.4% of the GP-to-control gap in Pythia-1B (L7+L10+L11) and 89.2% in Llama-3.2-1B (top-5 layers); four heads give 87.6% recovery, but zero-ablating DLA heads does not remove fixation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label fixation is mediated by a sparse but redundant attention circuit that overrides a correct mid-layer encoding.

record.code_released: Will be released; no URL stated.
record.problems: The authors note that the persistence-at-scale result relies on a single 8B model family, that instruction-tuned results cover only two models, and that the circuit differs across architectures. Bootstrap CIs may have below-nominal coverage with 10–20 clusters, as the authors acknowledge.
record.rows_left_out: Not cataloged: the paper's broader GP-versus-control task accuracy tables, threshold and dose-response results, multiclass and multi-token experiments, calibration, and format-ablation findings. They concern label fixation rather than any behavior named by V1–V7. Relevant set-level and circuit findings are recorded in R1–R10.

untested.parts: No identification of induction heads or previous-token-head composition; patched heads (L10-H5, L8-H0, L7-H2, L10-H4) are not characterised as induction heads.
No training checkpoints, loss curves or formation timing.
No token-index ICL measurement or share attributed to induction heads.
No search for induction-behaviour heads across models; cross-model results concern label fixation.
Varies prompt demonstrations, not training data or setup.
Does not compare induction heads with other heads (e.g. function-vector heads) as carriers of few-shot task learning.

record.verdict_notes: Rows correctly link to none. R1–R3 are aggregate ranges read from text/Figure 4 with no baseline stated. Zero-shot and control baselines exist elsewhere (Table 4), but not for these conditions. R9 lacks a numeric value. The 'sharpens the induction-heads framework' remark is a reinterpretation of the copy target, not evidence on V1 or V6. The sharp k=7→8 transition is at inference, not in training, so it is not V2/V7 evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify or test induction heads, previous-token-head composition, or the specified copying pattern.
No training-time measurements, loss curve, or token-index in-context-learning trajectory.
Does not estimate what share of token-index in-context learning in large transformers is carried by induction heads.
Tests label fixation across models, not the occurrence of heads with induction behavior across families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Varies demonstration-label conditions, not training data or training setup governing induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Does not compare mechanisms for few-shot task learning against induction heads as carriers of copying.
Does not study the number or timing of training transitions in induction-head formation.
